scope: Naive first-available-worker FIR batches; matched direct M4-only reference; no placement cost model
notes: Per-batch ready-list initialization is included in parallel elapsed time.
Both per-core kernel choices are calibrated separately; job placement ignores costs.
Sequential timing uses direct filter calls without queue or per-job tracing overhead.
Primary speedup uses fastest measured M4-only clock and kernel for the same workload.
Fixed-clock speedup is retained separately and must not be confused with beating the fastest sequential reference.
Diagnostic traced batch times are separate from primary speedup measurements.
Earlier exploratory sweeps excluded ready-list initialization and are superseded by these final sweeps.
First-available workers claim next job under a short hardware lock; no assignment cost model.
Sequential reference uses fastest tested direct M4 kernel on identical shared buffers.
Per-core kernel selection is calibrated outside timing; placement does not use predicted job costs.
Primary timings have per-job tracing disabled; separate traced batches prove overlap.
Parallel elapsed includes ready-list initialization, publication, IPC wake, claiming, computation, imbalance, and completion.
Preparation, calibration selection, reference checks, and output validation are outside batch timing.
